info.name: ForgeOps POC - SAML 2.0 SP-Initiated SSO
info.description:
Mirrors ./saml-sso-flow.sh: 1) authenticate the demo user to get an AM session, 2) hit the SimpleSAMLphp SP's authenticate.php which redirects to AM's SSORedirect endpoint with a SAMLRequest, 3) present the AM session cookie at that URL so AM issues an auto-submit HTML form containing a SAMLResponse, 4) extract and POST that SAMLResponse to the SP's ACS endpoint (completes the SSO handshake), 5) verify the SP now has an authenticated, federated session.

Before running:
- AM's hosted IdP and the SP must already be in the same circle of trust (poc-cot) -- see INSTALLATION.md / the SAML rebuild runbook. Circle-of-trust membership must use the 'entityId|saml2' format (not '|IDPRole'/'|SPRole') or AM rejects the request with 'Issuer in Request is not valid'.
- Disable 'SSL certificate verification' in Postman Settings > General, since AM/the SP use a self-signed cert (matches the -k in the shell script).
- Unlike the WSL curl script, no --resolve trick is needed here -- Postman runs on Windows, which already has the poc.example.com hosts entry.
- Requests run in order (Runner, or click Send top-to-bottom) -- each step feeds variables (and cookies, via Postman's cookie jar) into the next. Make sure Postman's cookie jar is enabled so the SP's session cookies from step 2 carry through to steps 4-5.
- AM's auto-submit form line-wraps the base64 SAMLResponse using literal HTML character references (
) instead of real whitespace; step 3's test script HTML-unescapes and strips it before use, mirroring a bug fix already applied to saml-sso-flow.sh.

request.description: Simulates the demo user logging in directly to AM. Returns a tokenId which becomes the AM session cookie (iPlanetDirectoryPro) presented to the IdP endpoint in step 3.

IMPORTANT: must NOT follow redirects (see protocolProfileBehavior.followRedirects = false) -- the AuthnRequest URL is in the Location header, not a followed body. The SP also sets its own session cookies here (Postman's cookie jar picks these up automatically and replays them in steps 4-5).

exec: // SimpleSAMLphp sends either a raw 302/303 with a Location header, or an
// HTML meta-refresh/JS bounce page (200) -- both are valid ways to carry
// the AuthnRequest via the HTTP-Redirect binding; handle either.

item.name: 3. Present AM session cookie at AM's SSO endpoint

request.description: AM validates the SAMLRequest's Issuer against the circle of trust and, if trusted, returns an auto-submit HTML form containing a base64 SAMLResponse. A 4xx/5xx here almost always means the IdP/SP aren't in the same circle of trust correctly (check the 'Issuer in Request is not valid' note in the collection description).

exec: pm.test('AM did not reject the SAML request', () => {
pm.test('SAMLResponse present in AM response', () => pm.expect(samlMatch).to.not.be.null);

item.name: 4. POST SAMLResponse to the SP's ACS endpoint

request.description: Completes the SSO handshake. acs_action_url is taken from the form AM returned in step 3 (falls back to nothing if step 3 didn't populate it -- re-run step 3 if this is empty). A 200/303 here means the SP accepted and validated the assertion.

This SP image doesn't ship the 'admin' module (module.php/admin/test/* 404s). With an active session, SimpleSAMLphp instead serves its status page directly (HTTP 200, showing the federated attributes) rather than redirecting back to AM -- relies on the SP session cookies Postman picked up in step 2/4.
